# Latin phrases in English and Swedish — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/latin-phrases.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/latin-phrases.ttl`](../decks/latin-phrases.ttl) · **Cards:** 77 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

77 Latin phrases still used in both English and Swedish, from ad hoc and carpe diem to status quo and vice versa. The Latin phrase on the front, its meaning in English and Swedish on the back, with the literal sense or origin as a note where it helps. Every phrase has an entry in Dictionary.com and in a Swedish reference work (Svenska Akademiens ordlista, Svensk ordbok or Nationalencyklopedin) and is recorded in Wikidata; the meanings are written for this deck, using the conventional translation where a phrase has one, and checked against those dictionaries and Wiktionary.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0-1.0. Its only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data (items and lexemes) is CC0. Selection: the dictionaries (SAOL, Svensk ordbok, NE, Dictionary.com) were used only as a yes/no filter on a candidate list the authoring agent wrote independently (all 216 candidates are named under Selection: the 77 cards, the 14 exclusions and the candidates that failed); no item was taken from their word lists, so no selection or arrangement of theirs is reproduced. Wording: the English and Swedish meanings and the notes are the authoring agent’s own wording of facts about the phrases, except that where a phrase has an established, non-original translation or fixed Swedish equivalent, that conventional rendering is used as a fact of the language rather than as any dictionary’s expression. This applies to a priori (“independent of experience”, “oberoende av erfarenhet”); ad infinitum (“i det oändliga”); ad libitum (“efter behag”); alter ego (“a second self”, “ett andra jag”); anno Domini (“in the year of our Lord”, “i Herrens år”); ante meridiem (“before noon”, “på förmiddagen”); ars longa, vita brevis; bona fide; carpe diem (“seize the day”, “fånga dagen”); caveat emptor; cogito, ergo sum; cum grano salis (“med en nypa salt”); e pluribus unum; errare humanum est; ex gratia (“as a favour”); ex officio (“å ämbetets vägnar”); festina lente; honoris causa (“för hederns skull”); in medias res (“mitt in i händelserna”); in memoriam; in vino veritas; in vivo (“in a living organism”); ipso jure (“by the law itself”); mens sana in corpore sano; nota bene (“märk väl”); o tempora, o mores! (“o tider, o seder!”); ora et labora; panem et circenses; per capita (“per person”); post meridiem (“after noon”, “på eftermiddagen”); primus inter pares; pro forma (“för formens skull”); quod erat demonstrandum (“vilket skulle bevisas”); requiescat in pace (“may he or she rest in peace”, “må han eller hon vila i frid”); rigor mortis (“likstelhet”); sic transit gloria mundi; tabula rasa (“ett oskrivet blad”); and veni, vidi, vici. No definition or explanatory wording was copied from SAOL, Svensk ordbok, NE or Dictionary.com (all rights reserved) or from the English and Swedish Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0); backs that had followed a definition or a Wiktionary gloss list too closely were reworded (quality-control rounds 1 and 3; the list above was completed in round 4). These sources, and Folkets lexikon (CC BY-SA 2.5) and Korp, which were tried and contributed nothing, are verification sources only, so their licences place no conditions on the deck. Quotations: the evidence in this provenance report quotes the sources briefly, verbatim and with the source named, to show what each one says about a card. These quotations are made under the quotation right (upphovsrättslagen 22 § for the Swedish works; fair use for the American ones), are kept to the minimum needed, and remain the property of their owners: they are not part of the deck’s cards and are not covered by the deck’s CC0 dedication or by the licence of the repository that holds this report. Wiktionary quotations are attributed to the English or Swedish edition and its contributors under CC BY-SA 4.0.

## Method

1. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund’s direction, with machine checks against the sources and three independent AI review rounds (factual accuracy; language and translation; licensing, attribution and documentation); the cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. Candidates. The authoring agent wrote a list of Latin phrases it judged to be in current English or Swedish use, from its own general knowledge; with duplicates and single words removed it holds 216 multi-word phrases. No list was copied from any source.
3. Swedish use. Each candidate was looked up in SAOL and Svensk ordbok through the svenska.se search API (https://svenska.se/api/search/saol and /api/search/so, parameters q, size=10, exactMatch=true), searching for the whole phrase and for each of its words longer than two letters, and keeping a hit when the phrase is the headword (field ortografi) or an idiom (field idiom) of a returned article. Each candidate was also looked up in Nationalencyklopedin at https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/lång/<phrase with spaces as hyphens>, keeping a hit when the page has an article title (reader-title heading); the title and opening text were saved. A missing NE article means only that no page exists at that URL slug: NE returns the same error page for a slug that does not exist at all as for a phrase it may treat under another title, so a “no” from NE is not proof that NE never mentions the phrase.
4. English use. Each candidate was looked up at https://www.dictionary.com/browse/<phrase with spaces as hyphens> without following redirects: HTTP 200 means the phrase has its own entry (its meta description, which carries the first definition, was saved); a 301 redirect to another word or a 404 means it has none. Merriam-Webster, Cambridge and Collins refused automated requests (HTTP 403), so Dictionary.com is the English dictionary of record.
5. Wikidata. Each candidate was searched with the Wikidata API (wbsearchentities, type item and type lexeme, languages la, en and sv) and the matching entities fetched with wbgetentities (labels, aliases, descriptions, claims, lemmas, senses). For each card the item that represents the phrase itself was chosen by hand (for example Q190273 for carpe diem rather than artworks named after it); where no such item exists, English or Swedish lexemes with the phrase as lemma serve instead.
6. Wiktionary. The English and Swedish Wiktionary wikitext of each candidate was fetched with action=raw and its definition lines kept, for checking meanings only.
7. Other avenues tried and not used: a first SAOL/SO pass searched only the whole phrase and missed idioms filed under one of their words (for example per capita under capita in SO), so the word-by-word search above replaced it; a Wikidata SPARQL query for lexemes timed out (HTTP 504), so the API search was used instead; Folkets lexikon (the KTH Swedish–English dictionary, CC BY-SA 2.5) was downloaded as XML from https://folkets-lexikon.csc.kth.se/folkets/folkets_sv_en_public.xml and matched only four of the first 134 candidates (ad notam, alter ego, nota bene, vice versa), too few to serve as a usage criterion; frequency counts in Språkbanken’s Korp news corpora (API https://ws.spraakbanken.gu.se/ws/korp/v8/, corpus list from /info) were too small and noisy (names of series and bands) to serve as one either. The Korp count requests themselves were not recorded verbatim when they were run, so they are not listed under Queries; the URLs that were recorded are. None of these avenues contributed anything to the deck.
8. Selection. A candidate was kept if it has an entry in Dictionary.com and in at least one of SAOL, Svensk ordbok or NE, then the exclusions listed under Selection were applied (non-Latin phrases, names and titles, a disputed subject, senses that differ between the languages, no Wikidata entity).
9. Writing the cards. Front: the phrase in Latin as Dictionary.com, SAOL, SO and NE spell it (lower case, j in de jure, ipso jure and res judicata, capital D in anno Domini, the commas of cogito, ergo sum and veni, vidi, vici). Back: a short meaning in English and in Swedish. Where a phrase has an established, conventional translation or fixed Swedish equivalent — a fact of the language that every dictionary repeats, such as “I came, I saw, I conquered”, “skynda långsamt” or “å ämbetets vägnar” — the back uses it; otherwise the meaning is the authoring agent’s own wording, and no dictionary definition or explanatory wording was copied (backs that had come too close to a definition were reworded in quality-control rounds 1 and 3). Where a phrase has a narrower sense in one language the back gives the sense common to both. A back note gives the literal sense, the origin (author, motto, field), an abbreviation or the contrasting phrase when it helps; every fact in a note is stated by at least one of NE, Dictionary.com, Wiktionary, SAOL, SO or Wikidata in the card’s evidence.
10. Cross-checking. Every card’s meaning was compared with the definitions saved from the Swedish source(s), Dictionary.com and Wiktionary; the evidence of each card quotes what those sources returned on 2026-10-04 (generated from the saved responses, trimmed). Wikidata label checks were added wherever the front, or a back text, is exactly (same case and punctuation) a Wikidata label or alias of the chosen item in that language (when only the multilingual “mul” label matches, one check is written for Latin, which the builder compares with mul labels too); they are run against live Wikidata by authored_decks.py check/build. After the review rounds, every back and note was compared mechanically with every quoted source text of its card (any segment of three or more words between commas or semicolons, and any whole back; before comparing, case and punctuation are normalised, parenthesised abbreviations such as “(a.m.)” or “(RIP)” are removed, a leading article is ignored and “/” in a source is read as “or”/“eller”). The first run (round 3) compared whole backs including the parenthesis and only backs of two or more words, and so missed six cards; the corrected run (round 4) flags only the conventional translations listed under Licensing. The quotations in the evidence were shortened to what confirms the card (gloss, literal sense, origin), with omissions marked “…” and NE’s pronunciation keys replaced by “[…]”.

## Selection

The deck holds the multi-word Latin phrases, from a candidate list of 216, that have their own entry in Dictionary.com (English) and appear in at least one Swedish reference work — as a headword or idiom in Svenska Akademiens ordlista or Svensk ordbok, or as a Nationalencyklopedin article — and that Wikidata records as an item or lexeme. 91 candidates met the dictionary criteria; 14 were then left out: “a cappella”: Italian, not Latin (NE: “italienska, egentligen ’i kapellstil’”). “lingua franca”: Italian, not Latin (NE: “italienska, egentligen ’frankernas språk’”). “homo sapiens”: a scientific species name, not a phrase of general use. “agnus dei”: a liturgical text and title (NE: a litany sung at the breaking of bread). “dies irae”: the title of a hymn of the requiem mass. “de profundis”: NE treats it as the Latin title of Psalm 130. “dominus vobiscum”: a liturgical greeting rather than a phrase used in everyday English or Swedish. “opus dei”: the NE article is about the Catholic organisation of that name. “pax romana”: the name of a historical period, not a phrase used of anything else. “pro patria”: the NE article is about the Swedish charitable society Pro Patria, not the phrase, so the Swedish criterion is not really met. “in corpore”: the Swedish sense (SAOL, SO: “med fulltalig representation”, as a whole body) differs from the English one (Dictionary.com: “in body; in substance”), so one back would mislead one of the two audiences. “jus primae noctis”: it names an alleged right whose historical existence is disputed (NE: “… förekommit i Europa är omstridd”). “ecce homo”: Wikidata has no item or lexeme for the phrase itself (only artworks titled so), so the card would have no CC0 content source. “terra firma”: Wikidata has no item or lexeme for the phrase (only unrelated works and the general item “land”), so the card would have no CC0 content source. Single Latin words (veto, alibi, ergo) and abbreviations (e.g., i.e., etc.) are outside the deck. Phrases that did not meet the criteria include several well-known ones (alea iacta est, et cetera, per se, quid pro quo, sui generis, vox populi, habeas corpus): either Dictionary.com has no entry for them or none of SAOL, SO and NE had a matching headword, idiom or article at the URL tried; they can be added if a later check finds them. Candidates not meeting the dictionary criteria: a capella, a contrario, ab absurdo, ad absurdum, ad acta, ad astra, ad fontes, ad lib, ad nauseam, ad notam, ad personam, ad undas, ad usum, ad usum delphini, alea iacta est, alea jacta est, annus horribilis, ante portas, conditio sine qua non, corpus juris, cui bono, cum laude, de lege ferenda, de lege lata, deo gratias, divide et impera, do ut des, dum spiro spero, eo ipso, et alii, et cetera, et tu brute, ex libris, ex nihilo, ex nunc, ex post facto, ex tempore, ex tunc, ex ungue leonem, ex voto, exempli gratia, fiat lux, habeas corpus, hannibal ante portas, homo homini lupus, id est, in absentia, in abstracto, in blanco, in camera, in casu, in concreto, in dubio pro reo, in extremis, in flagranti, in hoc signo vinces, in loco parentis, in natura, in nuce, in persona, in pleno, in praxi, in spe, in statu nascendi, in toto, in vacuo, inter alia, inter nos, ius primae noctis, lapsus linguae, lege artis, lex talionis, magna cum laude, nemo propheta in patria, nihil obstat, non compos mentis, non plus ultra, non sequitur, numerus clausus, opus magnum, pater familias, pax vobiscum, per annum, per aspera ad astra, per definitionem, per diem, per procura, per se, post festum, post mortem, post partum, post scriptum, pro anno, pro bono, pro domo, pro et contra, pro memoria, pro mille, pro primo, pro rata, pro rata temporis, pro tem, pro tempore, quid pro quo, sapere aude, senatus populusque romanus, sensu lato, sensu stricto, si vis pacem para bellum, stante pede, status nascendi, stricto sensu, sub rosa, sub specie aeternitatis, sui generis, sui juris, summa cum laude, summa summarum, tempora mutantur, tempus fugit, tertium non datur, ultima ratio, urbi et orbi, vade mecum, vox populi.

## Queries

**SAOL lookup of each candidate phrase and of each of its words longer than two letters (headword or idiom match).** (Svenska Akademiens ordlista (SAOL), 14th edition, on svenska.se)

```
GET https://svenska.se/api/search/saol?q=<phrase or word>&size=10&exactMatch=true   (example: https://svenska.se/api/search/saol?q=ad+hoc&size=10&exactMatch=true)
```

**Svensk ordbok lookup, same procedure.** (Svensk ordbok utgiven av Svenska Akademien (SO), on svenska.se)

```
GET https://svenska.se/api/search/so?q=<phrase or word>&size=10&exactMatch=true   (example: https://svenska.se/api/search/so?q=capita&size=10&exactMatch=true)
```

**Nationalencyklopedin article for each candidate (hit = page with an article title).** (Nationalencyklopedin (NE.se), encyclopedia articles)

```
GET https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/l%C3%A5ng/<phrase, spaces as hyphens>   (example: https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/l%C3%A5ng/carpe-diem)
```

**Dictionary.com entry for each candidate, redirects not followed (200 = own entry; meta description saved).** (Dictionary.com (based on the Random House Unabridged Dictionary))

```
GET https://www.dictionary.com/browse/<phrase, spaces as hyphens>   (example: https://www.dictionary.com/browse/ad-hoc)
```

**Wikidata items and lexemes whose label or lemma is the phrase (run for languages la, en and sv, types item and lexeme).** (Wikidata)

```
GET https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities&type=<item|lexeme>&language=<la|en|sv>&strictlanguage=<1 for items, 0 for lexemes>&search=<phrase>&format=json&limit=20
```

**Fetch the matching entities.** (Wikidata)

```
GET https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities&ids=<up to 40 ids>&format=json&props=labels|aliases|descriptions|claims|sitelinks&languages=la|en|sv|mul
```

7 rounds, 52 findings: 42 fixed, 1 rejected after checking, 9 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (81 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.
